sources.issuer: United States Department of State, International Boundary Study42
facts: Treaty signed1October1960; protocol signed13October1961 with detailed boundary/pillar maps replacing original treaty maps.
ArticleVII2(4) follows Laisa,Molechaung,Gayang,Nampaung to Taping then up Taping to a ridge west of Kuli confluence.
ArticleVII2(5–7) describes Kuli/Husa–Namwan versus Taping watersheds, then Kindit/NamWa/NamSah and historical Namwan/Shweli courses; part expressly depends on treaty maps.
Original treaty maps:1:250000 general and1:50000 selected. ArticleVIII distinguishes river-channel rules; it does not authorize replacing the treaty line with a contemporary river axis.
limits: U.S. official study is a primary government analysis reproducing treaty text, not the original bilateral map annex.
1964 statement that protocol maps were not public is historical, not a finding of current inaccessibility.
No candidate centre has been matched to a surveyed pillar/course/watershed segment. Datum unverified.
